description: Writing ArcPy scripts for ArcGIS Pro that run correctly the first time, covering arcpy.da cursors in with blocks, environment settings (workspace, outputCoordinateSystem, overwriteOutput), licence levels and extensions, cloning arcgispro-py3, edit sessions with arcpy.da.Editor for versioned data, and the classic errors. Use it when asked to "write an ArcPy script", "automate this in Pro", "loop through features", "update a field with a cursor", "batch geoprocess", or when a script fails with ERROR 000725, a schema lock or "cannot update outside an edit session".
name: arcpy-scripting

description: Choosing and checking coordinate reference systems so distances, buffers and areas come out right, covering projected vs geographic CRS, Texas state plane and EPSG:3081/3083, UTM, equal-area, NAD83 vs WGS84, NAVD88 and geoids, lat/lon axis order and US survey feet. Use it when asked to "reproject", "buffer by 500 ft", "measure distance", "calculate acreage", "what EPSG should I use", or when coordinates look swapped, land in the wrong place or have the wrong units.
name: crs-and-datums

description: Reading and safely working with Esri enterprise geodatabases (SDE) on Oracle, SQL Server and PostgreSQL, covering versions, reconcile and post, branch vs traditional versioning, a protected DEFAULT, domains and subtypes, relationship classes, attribute rules, archiving, ST_Geometry vs SDO_GEOMETRY vs SQL Server geometry, and versioned views vs base tables. Use it when asked to "query the SDE", "edit the enterprise geodatabase", "reconcile and post", "what do these codes mean", "why does SQL show different rows than ArcGIS Pro", or before touching any versioned or registered table.
name: enterprise-geodatabases

description: Finding and using satellite imagery through STAC APIs, covering searches by collection, bbox, datetime and eo:cloud_cover, Sentinel-2 L2A and Landsat Collection 2 Level-2, cloud masking with the SCL band and QA_PIXEL, scale factors and offsets, NDVI and other indices with the right bands per sensor, mosaics and composites, and the Planetary Computer and Earth Search endpoints. Use it when asked to "find Sentinel-2 or Landsat imagery", "search STAC", "get a cloud-free image", "calculate NDVI", "mask clouds", "make a median composite", or when index values fall outside -1 to 1.
name: imagery-and-stac

description: Processing lidar point clouds (LAS, LAZ, COPC, EPT) with PDAL, covering JSON pipelines, ASPRS classification codes (2 ground, 6 building, 7 low noise, 9 water, 18 high noise), ground filtering with filters.smrf and filters.pmf, density checks, CRS and vertical datum in LAS headers, and reading the USGS 3DEP EPT bucket. Use it when asked to "make a DTM or DSM from lidar", "classify ground", "remove noise", "check point density", "what are these classification codes", "get 3DEP lidar for my area", or "convert LAZ to COPC".
name: lidar-with-pdal

description: Work with linear referencing (LRS) data, meaning routes with measures, point and linear events, mileposts and DFO, calibration and dynamic segmentation, and run QC for gaps, overlaps, reversed measures, events past the route end and recalibration drift. Use when someone mentions route and measure, from/to measures, mile points, event tables, an LRS check or LRS QC, locating assets along routes, or segments that do not line up.
name: linear-referencing

description: Making maps and data deliverables that meet a spec, covering layout elements (scale bar, north arrow where meaningful, legend, data sources and dates, CRS note), symbology and classification methods (natural breaks, quantile, equal interval), colour-blind safe palettes, ISO 19115 and FGDC metadata basics, and checking a delivery spec for CRS, formats, field renames and required metadata. Use it when asked to "make a map", "export a PDF", "symbolize this layer", "pick colours", "write metadata", "package the deliverable", "send this to the district", or before handing any map or data to someone else.
name: maps-and-deliverables

description: Find, vet and cite open GIS data (parcels, lidar, elevation, flood zones, census boundaries, hydrography, imagery, roads) by searching a curated registry before the web, checking licence, terms, attribution, coverage and update cadence, and recording provenance. Use when someone asks "where can I get ... data", "is there open/free data for ...", "find a shapefile, layer or basemap for ...", or "can we use this dataset and how do we credit it".
name: open-data-sourcing

description: Working correctly with rasters and elevation models in GDAL, rasterio and ArcGIS, covering resampling choices, nodata, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (overviews, tiling, gdal_translate -of COG), DEM slope, aspect and hillshade with the right z-factor, zonal statistics pitfalls (cell alignment, all-touched) and mosaicking tiles. Use it when asked to "make a hillshade", "calculate slope", "resample", "reproject a raster", "convert to COG", "mosaic DEM tiles", "zonal statistics by parcel", or when slope values look absurd or a raster has holes or edge stripes.
name: raster-and-terrain

description: Convert Word, PDF or Excel SOPs, procedures, checklists and manuals into context-pack entries (Markdown with YAML front matter) without losing a step, threshold or exception, then prove the result with a step-by-step comparison and a fresh-reader test before a person signs off. Use when someone asks to turn a procedure document, SOP, work instruction, QC checklist or workflow spreadsheet into context pack entries or agent-readable instructions.
name: sop-conversion

description: Quality-checking spatial data before it is used or delivered, covering invalid geometry (self-intersections, ring orientation), null and empty shapes, duplicates, mixed geometry types, slivers, gaps and overlaps, topology, schema and domain checks, and CRS sanity, and what to fix, flag or send to the data owner. Use it when asked to "QA this layer", "validate geometry", "check for duplicates", "fix invalid polygons", "is this data clean", or before handing any result to someone else.
name: spatial-data-qa

description: Getting attribute joins and spatial joins right, covering key types, leading-zero padding (CSJ, county FIPS, ZIP), case and whitespace, null keys, one-to-many row blowups, intersects vs within vs contains, boundary effects and reporting the match rate honestly. Use it when asked to "join a table to a layer", "spatial join points to polygons", "match records by ID", "why didn't my join match", "low match rate", or when a join returns too many rows.
name: spatial-joins-and-keys

description: Write correct, fast, read-only spatial SQL for PostGIS, Oracle Spatial (SDO_RELATE, SDO_WITHIN_DISTANCE) and SQL Server (STIntersects, geography), covering intersects, within a distance, nearest, bounding-box filters, areas and lengths. Use when asked to query a spatial database, find features inside or near something, write or fix a spatial SQL query, or when a query is slow, gives distances in the wrong units, or is refused by sql_select.
name: spatial-sql

description: How to work through a governed GIS server such as Columbus, from the first whoami call to describe, sample and query a dataset, pass ws:// handles between tools, read checks, wait for approvals and handle refusals or hidden fields, and how to work with tables of a million rows or more and build a local project database (keys, indexes, joins in SQL). Use it at the start of any GIS session with Columbus tools, or when someone asks to "query a layer", "pull features", "run a query on roads", "join these tables", "build a project database", "why was this refused" or "what do these checks mean".
name: working-with-columbus

description: Apply Strunk's timeless writing rules to ANY prose humans will read—documentation, commit messages, error messages, explanations, reports, or UI text. Makes your writing clearer, stronger, and more professional.
name: writing-clearly-and-concisely
